alt: Design agentic systems. Guide your team.. Build a working system. Explain your decisions. Develop your reasoning through continuous feedback.  30 live hours plus independent work.  Explore the open cohort.
Start with the job. An expense assistant should help resolve a request. “Use an agent” does not explain the job.
Separate the fixed rules. A spending limit can be checked in code. A model does not need to reinterpret it on every run.
Find the uncertain decision. An unclear description may need interpretation or another question. Name what information would resolve it.
Bound the action. Preparing a recommendation and authorising a payment carry different responsibilities. Define each permission.
Decide how to check it. Use cases with known outcomes, review ambiguous cases and test what happens when evidence is missing.
Review your own workflow. Which steps need interpretation? Which need tools? Which can stay deterministic?  Illustrative teaching example.
Choose for the job. A planner, checker and writer can have different needs. Start by naming the decision each one owns.
Define acceptable behaviour. What must this role get right? Which failure would make the output unusable?
Compare on your cases. Use representative inputs and the same acceptance criteria. Include difficult and incomplete cases.
Count the surrounding cost. Include retries, review time and failed work alongside model charges. A cheaper call can cost more overall.
Test the checker too. A second model can share mistakes. Compare its judgments with known cases and qualified human review.
Make the choice revisitable. Record the reason, the limitation and the evidence that would trigger a new comparison.  Illustrative model-selection review.
Compare a decision. Illustrative case: choose a model for drafting a service plan that must respect fixed constraints.
Start with the constraint. One candidate writes clearly but misses a required condition. Decide whether that failure is acceptable before looking at price.
Inspect the whole system. Can a deterministic check detect the omission? What happens after it is detected? Include the cost of that recovery.
Compare like with like. Use the same representative cases and criteria. Record latency, successful work, failures and review effort.
Explain the trade-off. “It is cheaper” leaves out the consequence. Explain what improves, what becomes harder and what remains uncertain.
Say what would change your mind. A decision is easier to review when the next piece of evidence is explicit. What would you test next?
A review starts with behaviour. Illustrative example: the checker rejects an output and the agent tries again. The same rejection repeats.
Ask the next question. What new evidence or valid option does the next attempt have? If nothing changes, why would it succeed?
Locate the decision. The checker identifies the failure. The workflow needs an explicit decision about recovery, stopping or human review.
Make a change you can test. Bound the attempts. Define the unresolved outcome. Record enough evidence to explain why the workflow stopped.
Run the difficult case again. Does it stop correctly? Can a reviewer understand the failure? What uncertainty remains?
Practise the reasoning. Build, explain, examine and revise through continuous feedback.  Design agentic systems. Guide your team. learning.thelivingcraft.ai
